Answer: C
Reason: The CT images demonstrate massive, diffuse dilation of the trachea and main bronchi with numerous large cystic spaces (diverticula), which is the pathognomonic appearance of Mounier-Kuhn syndrome (tracheobronchomegaly). The "cavities" seen on X-ray are actually these dilated airways, and the hilar opacity corresponds to the markedly enlarged central airways rather than a mass or lymphadenopathy.
